title: The Collapse of the Indus-Script Thesis: The Myth of a Literate Harappan Civilization

claims.normalized_claim: The Indus script is not a writing system encoding language but consists of non-linguistic symbols.

claims.not_understood: Being contradicted here is narrower than it sounds. The checks argue against the strong claim that the signs encode no language at all. They do not show what language the signs encode, or what any sign says. Entropy in the linguistic range is the kind of evidence a writing system should produce, but some non-linguistic systems can produce it too, and specialists still debate the entropy result itself. The program does not know which parts of the sign system, if any, are phonetic (sound-based), and it has no check of this claim on a corpus independent of the Mahadevan/ICIT lineage. What would change the picture: a positional and entropy check on a genuinely independent corpus, and a named specialist's account that engages the suffix and title-formula findings directly.

explanation_record.explanation_text: The program checked this claim against three pieces of evidence, and all three point the other way. First, published work by other researchers (Rao and colleagues, 2009) measured how predictable each sign is from the signs before it - a measure called conditional entropy. The Indus values fell inside the range seen for real language writing, and outside the range seen for non-linguistic symbol sets. Second, the program's own positional battery (Phase-43) found 20 signs that behave like word endings - they sit at the end of texts the way suffixes do. Third, the same battery found a fixed two-sign formula that opens inscriptions, the way a title or heading does. Non-linguistic emblem sets are not expected to show grammar-like habits of either kind. The claim also carries its own test on the record - it would be in trouble if the entropy data fell in the linguistic range and positional patterns rose above a random baseline - and that is the result the checks returned. On the strength of this, the program records the claim as contradicted. One caution belongs in the open: two of the three contradicting items come from the program's own test battery, run on corpora from one lineage (the Mahadevan/ICIT line). The published entropy result is the only one of the three that was produced entirely outside this program.

audit_note_2026_10_22.note: Framing note (spec-025 material audit, 2026-10-22): the published exchange does not support treating the linguistic question as settled. Sproat 2014 (Language 90(2):457-481, DOI 10.1353/lan.2014.0031, FULL TEXT) shows the published entropy measures do not discriminate real non-linguistic systems, and the measures that do classify place Indus largely via text length; Rao et al. 2010 (DOI 10.1162/coli_c_00030, FULL TEXT) claims inductive evidence only; the exchange closed in non-concession (Rao 2015 / Sproat 2015). The literature position is contested and unresolved. Supporting items: Parpola 2008 (FULL TEXT) and Vidale 2007 (quoted in FULL TEXT) reject Farmer's proof claim; Mukhopadhyay 2023 (DOI 10.1057/s41599-023-02320-7) partially vindicates the functional core at abstract level; Nair 2026 (FULL TEXT) is mixed and expressly does not resolve the question. Any status change is for the program's adjudication gate, not this note.

Condition F (dedicated final sets): holds — 7 TERMINAL_STRONG sign(s) against a permutation-null chance level of 0 (999 permutations, seed 43052). Condition O (opening formula): holds — the most frequent opening bigram (400, 740) recurs 179 times (dominance 0.0608 over B = 2942) against a chance level of 76 occurrences. Outcome: INCONSISTENT. Both conditions hold: positional structure of the kind the thesis denies is present in this compilation, and the caveat widens. The sensitivity population's run returned INCONSISTENT under the same battery. The parent claim's contradicted status stands as recorded; this outcome moves no verdict and is not a verdict on the Farmer-Sproat-Witzel thesis.
